questions.prompt: Explain how mRNA COVID vaccines lead to protective antibodies, step by step.
questions.explanation: Lipid nanoparticles carrying spike mRNA fuse with cells (ideally immune cells) → ribosomes translate spike protein → fragments displayed on MHC-2 (APC) → a matching B cell is selected (with helper T help) → clonal expansion into plasma cells (anti-spike antibodies that neutralize the virus) and memory cells.

questions.prompt: Describe how quorum sensing works and how an inhibitor could stop a pathogen from causing disease.
questions.explanation: Each bacterium releases a signal and has receptors for it; when enough cells are present, signal binds neighbors' receptors and they all switch on together (e.g., releasing toxins). An inhibitor binds the receptors without triggering them, so the bacteria never sense a quorum and never turn toxic, giving the immune system time to clear them.
